question: Where can three adjacent identical complete bare ordinary words B B B occur?
premises: B is a complete ordinary word without the reserved consecutive units r,y, not a marked continuation fragment or quote control.
Every sentence contains exactly one or two terms followed by its final predicate. A bare predicate is unary; a binary predicate has the explicit ry cause suffix.
Every sentence boundary is written: exactly three body blank cells, or a sentence-end o in the separately positioned margin. An ordinary line wrap does not close a sentence.
If the same B is used both as a term and as a property, both lexical entries must be shared and learned. Shape equality itself supplies neither meaning.
conclusion: Exactly one of the two seams inside the triple must be an explicitly written sentence boundary.
proof: With no sentence boundary inside the triple, all three ordinary B words belong to one sentence. If its final predicate is one of them, the third B cannot remain after it inside that sentence; if the third B is the final predicate, it is bare and unary but has at least two terms. If the predicate lies farther right, there are already at least three terms before it. All cases are illegal.
With boundaries at both seams, the middle B is a complete one-word sentence. Every predicate requires at least one explicitly written term, so this is illegal.

A boundary only at the first seam is possible as a window: the first B is the predicate of a sentence whose term lies to the left; the second and third B are term and property in the next sentence. A boundary only at the second seam is possible: the first pair is term plus property, and the last B is a term at the start of the next sentence. Appropriate outer words and closures are still required.
known_obligations: The qokedy, sheol, okaiin and chol triples were already known from old857 and the later noun-class review HIST:abcbdb9b97d06b19; this is not their discovery. None contains literal ry. No existing pixel or transcription packet was queried here, and no claim about actual gap widths is made. The fixed carrier would fail on any eligible triple whose two seams are independently bound as ordinary gaps under its explicit physical measure.
limits: Conditional on this exact physical grammar and complete-group working-unit binding. Not a grammatical meaning for any native B, not a global-bijection result, not a new native observation, and not a repair or rerun of the older noun-class writer.
